claim: Bioelectric observable layer (Phase B1) created in cell_sim/layer5_bioelectric/. Adds a Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz (GHK) Vmem estimator and a feature extractor, plus a single conditional injection of pools['VMEM_MV'] into trajectory snapshots when RealSimulatorConfig.enable_bioelectric is True. The flag defaults False; flag-off behavior is bit-identical to the v15 / v16 baselines (verified by the existing Phase 2 gex-off bit-identity regression test). The simulator's _step / _apply paths are NOT touched. No new dynamics rules are added; no MCC measurement is performed. Phase B1 is the smallest possible step toward a Levin-style bioelectric layer: get a derived membrane-voltage observable into the trajectory snapshots so a future Phase B3 detector variant can use it as a feature.
source_detail: Reproducible via the new test suite cell_sim/tests/test_bioelectric_infrastructure.py (15 tests, all passing). Sandbox suite went from 281 to 296 passing with the additions; the 281 baseline is unchanged. Bit-identity regression test_gex_off_bit_identity_against_committed_baseline at RUN_PHASE2_REGRESSION=1: 2/2 PASS in 80 s. Confidence value 'assumed' rather than 'measured' because Phase B1 is infrastructure with placeholder permeability ratios (P_K=1, P_Na=0.04, P_Cl=0.45 from B. subtilis-like bacterial defaults; Syn3A has no measured ion permeabilities). Extracellular reference concentrations come from the published Luthey-Schulten Syn3A simulation medium at cell_sim/data/Minimal_Cell_ComplexFormation/input_data/initial_concentrations.xlsx ('Simulation Medium' sheet: K=12.67mM, Na=19.38mM, Cl=19.90mM).
caveats: Permeability ratios are placeholders. Syn3A has no measured ion-channel permeabilities. Defaults come from B. subtilis-like bacterial values. A future Phase B2 / B3 effort would either fit them from simulator outputs or absorb them into a calibrated detector.

Syn3A's medium has K+ nearly equal inside (10 mM) and outside (12.67 mM), unlike typical bacteria with strong K+ gradients (200 mM in / 5 mM out). As a result, the GHK-derived Vmem at the simulator's resting state is small (single-digit positive mV) rather than the canonical bacterial -100 to -180 mV. This is a feature of JCVI-Syn3A's engineered minimal medium, not a bug. Any detector using Vmem as an essentiality feature must not assume a canonical bacterial baseline.

Intracellular Cl- is 0 in the Luthey-Schulten Syn3A initialization (the 'Intracellular Metabolites' sheet does not include Cl-). The estimator clamps [Cl-]_i to a 1e-6 mM floor to keep the GHK denominator finite; this is a workaround for missing data, not a measurement.

No proton motive force (PMF) contribution. Real bacterial Vmem is dominated by the F1F0 H+ ATPase. The Luthey-Schulten Syn3A model holds H+ at a sentinel infinity in metabolite_counts and does not track an explicit H+ gradient. Adding PMF as a Vmem driver is Phase B2 (dynamics) work; Phase B1 reports the GHK-from-K+/Na+/Cl- estimate without PMF.

The bioelectric framework here is classical, not quantum. The 'quantum biology speculation synthesis' note at experiments/quantum_biology_speculation/SYNTHESIS.md documents why classical bioelectric (Levin lab) is the published-evidence-supported framework for cellular computation; quantum frameworks are not. This layer is the scoped engineering follow-up to that synthesis.

Phase B1 produces NO MCC measurement. Wiring Vmem features into a v17 detector and measuring against v16 is Phase B3 work. The realistic expected outcome (per the synthesis) is marginal MCC improvement at most — Syn3A is single-compartment, and bioelectric edge is bigger in multi-cell systems. The honest scientific result if v17 ~= v16 ± noise is informative ('classical bioelectric features add little signal at single-cell scale'), not a failure.

Confidence value 'assumed' is the best fit in the invariant checker's allowed set {measured, inferred, estimated, assumed} for placeholder kinetic parameters. The GHK formula itself is well-established (Hille 2001); the parameter VALUES are bacterial defaults, not Syn3A measurements.
